title: UX Tutorial
subtitle: Orientation and step-by-step workflow walkthroughs
intro: Use this page when onboarding new staff or refreshing a specific process. Each walkthrough lists portal pages in a sensible order; open links in sequence or jump ahead. For full reference text, open Help or the printable manual in the repo.

roles.smsReaders: Customer-care operators, superadmin, and O&M / IT
roles.bridgeAdmins: superadmin, O&M / IT, and Nexus administer_cc

orientation.title: App orientation (first session)
orientation.description: How the portal is organized: home, country, navigation, and where to find documentation.
steps: Start at the Dashboard for a snapshot of sites, counts, and health indicators.
Confirm the country (and portfolio, if shown) in the header matches the data you intend to work on — APIs and currency are per country.
Use the left sidebar for day-to-day work: Operations (reports, financials), Customer Data, Commerce, and System (tables, export, Help).
Open Help for the full operating manual with searchable sections.
Return here anytime via System → Tutorial for guided walkthroughs.

lifecycle.title: New customer lifecycle (happy path)
lifecycle.description: End-to-end flow from registration through metering; align with your local SOPs.
steps: Register the customer FIRST — before any payment or installation. Registration issues the account number (e.g. 0042MAK) that the customer needs as the payment reference for the connection fee, so nothing else can start until this is done.

When the customer pays the connection fee or full readyboard fee by mobile money, the portal recognises the exact amount automatically and queues it for finance verification — no manual matching required. If the customer can't pay it in full, grant an advance instead (see the Advances walkthrough).

Run the commissioning wizard: look up the customer, fill details, then link the uGridPLAN connection (pole/PTB) — required, or Generate Contract stays blocked — capture the signature, and generate the bilingual contract and SMS.
Assign or confirm the meter and serial in the meter registry.
Use Customer Data for balances, charts, and transaction history (including any active advances).
Track funnel position on the Pipeline page.

If the issued account was used to test the meter, do not decommission it. On the customer page, Reset setup data keeps the person, the account number, and the meter. It deletes test payments and readings, then stamps connection and readyboard debt from the fees saved for that country. Save the real fees first. Type RESET and the account number, and give a reason. Superadmin, or O&M for their own country. Undo it from Mutations. Refused after 21 days, after 40 payments, or while an advance, financing agreement, or unmetered service is active.
lifecycle.commissionStepBn: Run the commissioning wizard: look up the customer, fill details, then link the uGridPLAN connection (pole/PTB) — required, or Generate Contract stays blocked — capture the signature, then generate the French Mionwa Generation contract and send the French SMS.

countryActivation.title: Country activation readiness (Benin / Zambia)
countryActivation.description: Resolve the commercial, site, metering, payment, firmware, and evidence gates before a field batch is released.
steps: Select the intended country in the CC header, open Provisioning → Operator walkthrough, choose the deployment site, and refresh the evidence. Never use another country's site code or database as a workaround.

If a site is missing, expand “Site missing from the list?” in the Operator walkthrough. The country lead supplies the official name, proposed unique three-letter code, province/district, deployment lead, go-live date, tariff/fees, metering site ID and uGridPLAN project ID if used. Engineering deploys the canonical country configuration before any downstream Sync or equipment-commissioning page is used.
Country lead/Finance approve the electricity tariff plus connection and readyboard fees. An authorized Finance/O&M user records the approved values on Tariffs.
Engineering configures the country metering organisation and per-site platform IDs. The country team confirms that the displayed sites match the real deployment.
Finance and Engineering validate real mobile-money provider samples and credentials before automatic ingestion and meter credit are enabled.
Firmware/Engineering registers an immutable signed OTA candidate for each site. Country O&M uses Guide & download to allocate exactly one test gateway and run the first canary.

Follow the Operator walkthrough through OTA, physical Batch validation, release approval, controlled batch provisioning, test-customer meter assignment, and actual-site commissioning. CC completes observable steps automatically and audits the operator confirmations for physical steps.

provisioning.title: Gateway provisioning & commissioning
provisioning.description: Take sealed factory-boot gateways through Starlink configuration, signed full-firmware OTA, and customer commissioning.
steps: A sealed factory-virgin gateway already has boot firmware. Do not open it, erase it, or use USB; it is programmed to recognize the approved provisioning LAN.

Open Provisioning → Operator walkthrough first and choose the deployment site. Continue only when its country and OTA gates are ready; then use the walkthrough's Guide & download action to download and fully extract the station. Read START_HERE_FACTORY_VIRGIN_GATEWAYS.md.

On a laptop on the same 1Meter provisioning network as the gateways (with internet to CC), run the station. When the terminal shows Open: http://localhost:8787, leave it open, open that address, select the deployment country, sign in, confirm the subnet, and Scan.
Pick the destination site, confirm its approved firmware release, and enter that site's exact Starlink SSID/password. CC records the SSID/config version but never the password.

Optional HQ validation: if the real site Starlink is unavailable, use the guided mirrored-network path to configure a controlled 2.4 GHz access point with the identical SSID/password and internet. This validates credential handoff and OTA, not the real site router or RF path.

For a candidate-only release, select exactly one unit. CC allocates its stable <SITE>-GW-#### identity, records it as the authorized test unit, delivers the bootstrap, and queues the signed OTA canary. After release approval, controlled batches can contain more units.
Keep every unit powered while CC shows live OTA progress (queued, in progress, succeeded, failed) for each gateway. Continue only when every Job is SUCCEEDED.
Download the meter-addressing kit. Address and label each meter individually, scan the combined RS485 string, then connect the sorted string to the gateway with power off.

Recommended for every batch: use Provisioning → Batch validation with a protected dummy load. Prove telemetry, consumption, zero-balance relay opening, synthetic payment, relay closing, and load restart; retain the evidence session ID.

Continue in the same Operator walkthrough after release approval: provision the controlled batch, reconcile telemetry, create or identify the test customer, use Assign Meter, run the payment/relay checks, and complete actual-site commissioning. Enter evidence references when requested; never enter a Wi-Fi password. The gateway name never changes.

Rollout, for every gateway and meter after site commissioning: the same day a gateway goes up, record it on its pole in Provisioning → Field install; wire the meters and confirm each serial in Fleet live; then use Assign Meter for each meter. Check the Meters page banner at the end of the day — a reporting meter that is not assigned is invisible and cannot be billed.

payments.title: Payments & reconciliation
payments.description: When SMS gateway data is missing or needs review, and how to trace credits.
steps: Record a missed mobile-money payment so 1PDB and SparkMeter stay aligned. The classifier auto-detects connection / readyboard fees by exact amount. Remaining electricity payments then pay unmetered-service fees (if enrolled), then advances, then kWh.
Work the verification queue for fees and deposits that need human matching — connection and readyboard fees auto-route here.
Browse Transactions for recent credits and amounts site-wide; the kWh balance column reflects the kWh balance after each row.
Drill into Customer Data for a specific account’s history, balance context, and any Active Advances panel.
Open the SMS inbox only after the sidebar is on one country. It lists inbound texts. It does not credit a customer.
A ledger correction on Customer Data is for superadmin and O&M only. It writes a raw row and does not change the balance. Use Record Payment for a real payment.

On Billing Priority, with one country selected, turn automatic power cutoff on or off. At zero credit a 1Meter-primary account loses power; a payment that restores credit turns it back on. Superadmin can save any country. O&M and finance can save only their own. The mutation log records who changed it and when. All countries cannot save.

Before a regulator inspection, hold the site on Billing Priority. Meters stay powered and the use is free. Connection and readyboard fees still collect. Electricity payments are saved and become kWh, at the tariff from the day they were paid, when you type BILL and the site code. To test billing on one meter during the hold, type BILL and that meter id. Hours before that switch stay free.

advances.title: Connection / readyboard advances
advances.description: Grant, manage, and reconcile fee advances when a customer can't pay the full amount up-front.
steps: Confirm the country fee amounts on the Tariffs page (Connection & Readyboard Fees card). These are the exact amounts the classifier looks for and the defaults pre-filled when granting an advance.

On the Advances page, click 'New advance', pick the customer, type (connection or readyboard), repayment fraction (default 50%), monthly fee % (premium), and upload the signed contract — the contract upload is required.

Once active, every electricity payment automatically siphons the repayment fraction toward the advance; the rest is credited as kWh. The ledger shows every grant, repayment, monthly fee accrual, contract replacement, and write-off.
Open Customer Data for the affected account to see the Active Advances panel with progress bar; deep-link back to the Advances page to edit or replace the contract.
Recognised fee payments still flow through Payment Verification — the advance is only repaid by subsequent electricity payments, not by the matched fee.

When contract/debt credit is positive, use manual debt-credit decisions on Advances: either Convert Debt Credit (to kWh/SparkMeter) or Refund Debt Credit. The system does not auto-convert these credits.

unmeteredService.title: Unmetered service (connected, no meter)
unmeteredService.description: Enroll connected customers who do not yet have a meter, accrue the monthly service fee, and let commissioning or meter assignment end it.
steps: Confirm the country monthly fee on Tariffs → Country fees (Lesotho default 50 LSL). Set it to 0 to block new enrollments.
On Unmetered Service (Commerce menu), enroll the account. Optionally record opening arrears for months already owed. One active enrollment per account.
Open Customer Data to see the amber Unmetered service strip. Top-ups pay this fee after onboarding fee debt and before advances or kWh.
When a meter is assigned or the customer is commissioned, enrollment ends automatically and monthly accrual stops. The ledger stays under the Ended filter.
For any other reason, use End enrollment on the Unmetered Service page. Do not leave connected-unmetered customers as an informal side arrangement.

reporting.title: Operations & reporting
reporting.description: Quarterly O&M, financial analytics, meter checks, and maintenance context.
steps: O&M Report: quarterly customer, consumption, and sales analytics.
Financial: ARPU trends, revenue by site, portfolio views.
Check Meters: compare primary vs check-meter signals where deployed.
Maintenance Log: ticket context linked to field work.

Customer Cohort: drill-down list of the individual customers behind the funnel — filter by site, customer type and payment status (not paid / partially paid / fully paid / terminated), sort, search by name or phone, and export to CSV for follow-up or call lists.

investorAnalytics.title: Investor analytics & portfolio KPIs
investorAnalytics.description: Portfolio-wide investor-grade metrics, multi-country KPIs, and Excel export.
steps: Open the Investor Analytics page under Operations in the sidebar. The Asset Register tab loads first — it shows every operational site with capacity, connections, customer mix, tariff (USD/kWh), and SCADA availability.

Switch to the KPI Time Series tab to view quarterly or monthly charts (connections, revenue, energy, ARPU) and a table with financial columns (OPEX, EBITDA, CAPEX). Use the Period and Site dropdowns to filter.
Use the Customers tab to drill into a specific site's customer list — filter by type (HH/SME/C&I), paginate through results, and see tariff plan, connection date, and last transaction.
Use the Transactions tab for site-level transaction history with USD conversion and date filtering. Click Export XLSX on the Asset Register tab to download a full investor workbook.

commerce.title: Tariffs, financing, and exports
commerce.description: Rate configuration, asset financing, unmetered service, and bulk extracts for analysis.
steps: Tariffs: site/concession rates that drive kWh conversion for new payments, plus country fees (connection, readyboard, unmetered service). An optional installation threshold, blank by default, treats amounts at or above it as a connection fee unless that account is exempt.
Financing: products, agreements, and ledger views.
Unmetered Service: enroll connected customers awaiting a meter; see the dedicated walkthrough.
Export: CSV/XLSX extracts for offline analysis (respect data-handling policy).

dataAudit.title: Data browsers, audit, and integrations
dataAudit.description: Raw views, change history, and uGridPlan sync status.
steps: Accounts: browse account rows and filters.
Tables: SQL table browser for advanced inspection.
Mutations: audit trail with revert where supported.
Sync: uGridPlan integration status and recent operations.

safetyOverride.title: Meter safety override — emergency relay cutoff
safetyOverride.description: How to force a meter's relay open in an emergency, and how to restore normal billing afterward.
steps: Open the Meter Registry and locate the target meter. The Safety column shows a green auto badge (normal) or red OVERRIDE badge (cutoff active).
Click the safety badge to open the two-step confirmation dialog. Select off (safety cutoff) and enter a mandatory reason — this is recorded in the audit log. Optional notes are saved alongside.
Click Confirm, then Confirm again within the 3-second countdown — this double-click prevents accidental cutoffs that would deprive a customer of paid-for electricity.

To restore normal billing, reopen the dialog and toggle back to auto. The relay will not immediately re-close; reconnection is handled by the normal billing cycle or the customer's next mobile-money top-up.

smsLog.title: SMS outbound log & delivery audit
smsLog.description: Inspect every outbound SMS and verify whether the carrier actually delivered it.
steps: Open the SMS Log under System → SMS Log. Every outbound SMS is automatically recorded — type, phone, account, message body, and two delivery statuses.
Filter by SMS type (balance / welcome / contract), success/failure, phone, account, or date range to narrow down what you need.

The Gateway column tells you whether the SMS host accepted the request (green Queued = success; red Failed = error). The CM.com column is the carrier delivery confirmation — Accepted means it reached the handset; Rejected or another status means the carrier refused or could not deliver it.
Click any row to expand the full message body, raw gateway URL, CM.com status timestamp and error code, and any internal error message.

smsInbox.title: SMS inbox
smsInbox.description: See inbound payment texts for one country, without crediting from this page.
steps: Set the sidebar to Lesotho, Benin, or Zambia. All countries asks you to pick one and does not open the Lesotho inbox by mistake.
Filter by account or outcome. Download CSV covers only the rows on screen. Phone-to-account lookup is read-only.
Editors open failed rows on SMS Formats → Unprocessed. Replay stays there. Benin replay does not credit unless an administrator has explicitly enabled it.
Everyone else follows the link to Record Payment. Do not type an account on the inbox in order to force a credit.

whatsappBridge.title: WhatsApp bridge
whatsappBridge.description: Link this country’s Customer Care phone. The QR is an admin page, not part of the inbox.
steps: Use a dedicated phone and a separate bridge process per country. Do not point Benin or Zambia at the Lesotho bridge.
Open System → WhatsApp bridge with the sidebar on that country. Scan WhatsApp → Linked devices → Link a device. The code rotates about every minute.
If the page says this country has no bridge URL, follow the Customer Care WhatsApp SOP. Starting the process and setting the secret is an operations step, not something the page does for you.

quiz.title: Knowledge check
quiz.intro: Eight questions on payments, the SMS inbox, the WhatsApp bridge, automatic power cutoff, resetting a test account, and free supply before inspection. Open an answer when you are ready.

items.q: A mobile-money text did not credit the customer. Where do you enter the payment?
items.a: Record Payment. The Customer Data ledger correction does not credit kWh or change the balance, and only superadmin and O&M can open it.

items.q: The sidebar says All countries. What does the SMS inbox do?
items.a: It asks you to pick Lesotho, Benin, or Zambia. It does not load a combined inbox, and it does not silently use Lesotho.

items.q: Who replays an unprocessed SMS so it can credit the account?
items.a: SMS format editors, from SMS Formats → Unprocessed. The inbox only links there. Benin replay stays off unless SMS_BN_REPLAY_CREDIT_ENABLED is set.

items.q: An installation threshold is set and this account is exempt. They pay exactly the connection fee. What is it?
items.a: Still a connection fee. Exemption skips only the threshold rule. An exact connection or readyboard amount still classifies as that fee until it is verified.

items.q: Where is the WhatsApp QR, and which phone does it link?
items.a: System → WhatsApp bridge, for the country in the sidebar. It is for superadmin, O&M / IT, and Nexus administer_cc. It does not fall back from Benin or Zambia to the Lesotho phone.

items.q: Who can turn on automatic power cutoff for Benin, and where is that recorded?
items.a: On Billing Priority, with the sidebar on Benin. Superadmin can save any country. O&M and finance can save only their own country. The mutation log stores who changed it, the old value, the new value, and when. Customers see a sentence on My Dashboard and cannot change it.

items.q: An issued account was used to test the meter. How do you clear the test payments and still keep that account number?
items.a: On the customer page, Reset setup data. Do not decommission. Save the real country fees first, because the reset stamps those amounts. Readyboard debt is stamped only if the customer takes a 1PWR readyboard. Type RESET and the account number. Superadmin, or O&M for their own country. Undo it from Mutations. Refused after 21 days, after 40 payments, or if an advance, financing agreement, or unmetered service is active.

items.q: A site is waiting on the regulator, but one meter should be billed so the tariff and relay can be tested. What do you do?
items.a: On Billing Priority, hold the site with HOLD and the site code. Then set that meter to Bill and type BILL plus the meter id. The rest of the site stays on free supply. Hours before the meter switch stay free. Clearing the site with BILL and the site code turns saved electricity payments into kWh at the tariff from the day they were paid.
